SvelteKit calls `load` from `+page.js`, `+page.server.js` and the like. A `load` that a `+page.svelte`, `+layout.svelte` or `+error.svelte` exports from its `<script context="module">` is the Sapper way and is never called.

The rule looks only at components in the routes of a SvelteKit project: below `kit.files.routes` of `settings.svelte` or of the Svelte configuration, else below `src/routes`, in a project that has `@sveltejs/kit`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-export-load-in-svelte-module-in-kit-pages": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"filename": "src/routes/+page.svelte", "packages": {"@sveltejs/kit": "2.5.0"}} */}

```svelte
<script context="module">
  export async function load({ fetch }) {
    return { items: await fetch("/api/items").then((it) => it.json()) };
  }
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"filename": "src/routes/+page.svelte", "packages": {"@sveltejs/kit": "2.5.0"}} */}

```svelte
<script>
  let { data } = $props();
</script>
```
